thread: alex (sales): FYI customer AcmeInc POC is intermittently failing on our Private endpoint. They see ~10-20 rps from their app and get TLS handshake errors + occasional 502s. Need quick triage.

lisa (acct): Customer reports DNS for private endpoint resolves to the VPC interface IP ok. Errors in their logs: "tls: unexpected certificate" and some 502s showing "connection reset by peer". They're blocked for demo tomorrow.

jamal (eng-networks): Can you paste a failing curl -v and the private endpoint FQDN? Also ask them to capture tcpdump on their side (ENI/NAT) for the timeframe. Suspect conntrack or NAT hairpin issues.

alex (sales): FQDN: acme-rw-private.redwood-internal.example (they used our private host). Here's their curl snippet:
```
curl -v --resolve "acme-rw-private.redwood-internal.example:443:10.5.7.12" https://acme-rw-private.redwood-internal.example/health
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Newsession Ticket (0x23)
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2)
* SSL certificate problem: certificate is not yet valid
```
lisa (acct): They say the cert appears valid in the console but curl shows not yet valid intermittently. Could be time skew on their NAT box or an edge proxy.

marta (eng-runtime): Our side logs show multiple entries around the same times:
```
[2024-10-15T18:12:04Z] proxy: tls handshake failed: tls: handshake failure (client hello sni="acme-rw-private.redwood-internal.example")
[2024-10-15T18:12:07Z] auth: connection closed by peer
[2024-10-15T18:12:07Z] rate: 429 apply: source_ip=192.0.2.45
```

marta (eng-runtime): Two things jump out: occasional 429s from our edge (per-source rate limits) and handshake failures. If the client's egress IP rotates (NAT pool, ephemeral), backend sees bursts from different IPs and may trigger our edge rate limiter. Also if connections are short-lived, TLS renegotiation can hit conntrack limits on their NAT.

jamal (eng-networks): For them: check conntrack entries and TIME_WAIT counts. Commands they can run on Linux bastion/NAT:
```
sudo conntrack -L | wc -l
netstat -tan | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l
sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
```
jamal (eng-networks): Ask them to also run `openssl s_client -connect 10.5.7.12:443 -servername acme-rw-private.redwood-internal.example -status` to confirm OCSP/expiry and SNI is sent.
acme-ops (customer): quick update from our infra lead: conntrack was ~65k entries (we cap at 65536), saw bursts up to the limit during load test. We'll increase nf_conntrack_max and retest.

sam (eng-oncall): Temporary mitigation from our side: disable aggressive per-src rate cutting for this customer's trial (we can whitelist their VPC egress CIDR on the edge for the POC). Need approval from infra security. Would also recommend long-lived keepalive from their app to reduce new TLS handshakes.
lisa (acct): Sales asks cost question: if we spin up a short-lived dedicated pool to avoid rate/conntrack issues, what's the pricing for a 2-week POC sandbox? Need rough number to share.

marta (eng-runtime): For ad-hoc Dedicated sandbox: we can do usage-based billing for two weeks; estimate ~ $X/day per GPU instance (send pricing offline). I'll DM finance for an exact quote and flag as POC discount.

jamal (eng-networks): Another durable fix: if they can put an AWS Interface VPC Endpoint (PrivateLink) to our service we can avoid NAT/egress IP churn entirely. That avoids firewall/egress concerns and keeps SNI intact. Requires customer infra work but is most robust.

acme-ops (customer): We're ok to try conntrack bump first. If that doesn't pass, we'll schedule PrivateLink with you. Can you confirm the hostname needs to match SNI exactly? Our infra team needs the exact config for the endpoint

jamal (eng-networks): Yes SNI must match the private host header. Use server_name = acme-rw-private.redwood-internal.example. For OpenSSL test use the `-servername` flag as above. Also ensure their firewall allows outbound 443 to our endpoint IPs. If they configure PrivateLink, we'll provide the service name and VPC Endpoint details.
infra-bot: Service:private-endpoint deployed to edge-zone-3 (ips: 10.5.7.10,10.5.7.11). cert: managed by Redwood, expires 2025-02-02T00:00:00Z. OCSP stapling: enabled.
lisa (acct): Security question from Acme: how do you handle certificate rotation and OCSP? They need an answer for their audit.

marta (eng-runtime): We manage TLS certs centrally, rotate before expiry, enable OCSP stapling on the edge. If customer requires, we support customer-provided certs for PrivateLink in Dedicated/Private deployments. I'll paste standard line for the questionnaire in the thread after.

marta (eng-runtime): (standard sec blurb) "Redwood manages TLS termination at the edge for hosted private endpoints; certificates are rotated proactively, OCSP stapling is enabled, and audit logs of certificate issuance/rotation are retained for enterprise customers via the Console. Customer-managed certs are available for Private deployments.",

- Customer increases nf_conntrack_max and retests (acme to confirm)
- If still flaky, customer enables PrivateLink endpoint and we whitelist ENI IPs (jamal + infra security)
